newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Typhoon Sally shuts down one airport in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Sally shuts down one airport in Taiwan.

text.p: Typhoon Sally gained strength on Sunday, forcing one of Taiwan's domestic airports to shut down and blocking part of the traffic in mountain areas, but officials did not expect the storm to cause major damage.
"Typhoon Sally is gaining strength and moving faster, but it's moving more towards the west instead of the north, which is good for Taiwan," said a Central Weather Bureau official.
Sally, the fourth typhoon to hit the island in 1996, was 310 km (192 miles) southwest of the most southern part of Taiwan at 10.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) on Sunday.

Strong wind forced the airport on southeastern offshore Lanyu island to close on Sunday morning, and torrential rains caused minor landslides, blocking part of the traffic in mountain areas in southern Taiwan, a disaster official said.
No other damage had been reported, the official added.

Sally was moving west at 30 kmh (18.6 mph) with maximum sustained winds of 172.6 kmh (107 mph) and gusts of up to 208.8 kmh (129.5 mph). It was expected to be 180 km (111 miles) west of southern Taiwan at 9.00 a.m. (0100 GMT) on Monday.
Gloria and Herb killed dozens of people and caused millions in damage when they roared across the island in late July and early August. The third typhoon, Lisa, caused little damage.
